exact_claim: A Dravidian language was spoken in or adjacent to the northwest during the period of Rigvedic composition and lent vocabulary into Old Indo-Aryan.
attested_or_hypothetical: ATTESTED family; the northwestern presence at that date is hypothetical
chronological_fit: CANNOT BE RUN AT VERIFIED LEVEL. No absolute date is establishable from anything retrieved (DE-M-027). Relative chronology only, on Arnold's strata, single-sourced (DEP-001).
geographical_fit: PASS, carried by one language. Nearest attested Dravidian lect to the northwest is Brahui at 393 km; without Brahui it is Kolami at 1,055 km (DE-M-023, DE-M-025).
contact_mechanism: PASS. Lexical borrowing under contact; Turner records the direction explicitly in 224 entries (DE-M-002).
positive_evidence: 224 CDIAL loan attributions, 15 with a Rigvedic simplex, 15 distinct lemmas, 21 tokens, 0.013% of the corpus (DE-M-009 to DE-M-011). Donor base: 76,303 DEDR reflex rows under 5,619 entries, 1,286 Proto-Dravidian starred forms, a 20-variety cognate-coded sample (DE-M-013, DE-M-014, DE-M-017).
contrary_evidence: The Rigvedic signal is small (DE-I-003). The geographic position depends on a single language whose own history is unsettled (DE-I-008). 29 of Turner's arrows cite no authority (DE-M-029).
independent_support: NONE that qualifies. DEDR and CDIAL are not independent of each other (DEP-011); DravLex is basic vocabulary and corroborates no individual etymology.
current_specialist_standing: NOT ESTABLISHABLE HERE (DE-I-009). Newest reachable opinion is Turner 1966.
diagnostic_predictions: Loans concentrate in later strata; show recipient-language adaptation; cluster in identifiable semantic domains; Brahui behaves as a relict.
falsifier: The stratum clustering dissolving on a larger candidate set; the loan etymologies being individually withdrawn in favour of Indo-Aryan-internal derivations; Brahui shown to be a late arrival with no northwestern Dravidian layer behind it.
reason: Passes on mechanism, geography and positive evidence. Does not pass on chronology at this record's standard, and the geographic pass is single-language. Both limits travel with the hypothesis rather than being dropped at the gate.

exact_claim: A Munda language proper was spoken in the northwest during Rigvedic composition and lent vocabulary into Old Indo-Aryan.
attested_or_hypothetical: ATTESTED family; the northwestern presence is hypothetical and unevidenced
chronological_fit: CANNOT BE RUN AT VERIFIED LEVEL. IH-119 is INHERITED-UNVERIFIED and is not used.
geographical_fit: ADVERSE. No attested Munda lect falls inside the northwestern envelope; nearest is Korku at 855 km (DE-M-022, DE-M-024). §4.P forbids reading modern distribution as prehistoric, so this weakens without closing.
contact_mechanism: PASS in principle; requires a presence the geography does not evidence.
positive_evidence: 55 CDIAL loan attributions, 5 with a Rigvedic simplex (DE-M-003, DE-M-009). Donor base: 1,096 attested reflexes across 12 languages, 127 reconstructed Proto-Munda etyma (DE-M-015).
contrary_evidence: The geography. And 85% of the 55 attributions cite Kuiper or PMWS, so they approximate one authority (DE-M-028).
diagnostic_predictions: Loans show Munda phonological shape and Munda-specific semantics; some Munda presence west of Korku is recoverable.
falsifier: Evidence of Munda-family speech west of Korku at any period - a toponym layer, an inscription, a secure Munda etymology in a northwestern language - would revive it.
proportional_space: Concise exclusion plus a historiographical note. Not an equal section.
reason: Fails on geography. The failure is scoped exactly as §4.E scopes it: it materially weakens a Munda-affiliated substrate explanation and does NOT transfer to HYP-E-003 or any other unattested prefixing language.

Giving Para-Munda parity with Dravidian was the recorded failure (IH-033); treating our inability to retrieve Witzel as evidence against him would be the mirror of it, and is refused. Under §6 this absence types as NOT ACCESSIBLE, the weakest kind of silence. The prefixing observation the proposal addresses is a real observation needing some explanation (IH-036).

positive_evidence: NOT MEASURABLE HERE. EM-21 reads zero (DE-M-019).

exact_claim: Masica's Language X: an unidentified donor, neither Indo-Aryan nor Dravidian nor Munda, behind part of the north Indian agricultural vocabulary.
attested_or_hypothetical: HYPOTHETICAL, and a residue rather than a donor with content.
geographical_fit: CANNOT GATE. Scope constraint inherited: IH-160 records that transplanting Language X to South India, Sri Lanka or the Ganges was REJECTED; it is Indus/northwest-specific.
positive_evidence: NOT MEASURABLE HERE. EM-22 reads zero (DE-M-019). Turner's own 101 entries of declared unknown origin (DE-M-018) are a different residue in a different corpus and are NOT used as a proxy.

exact_claim: Brahui is a relict of an earlier and wider Dravidian distribution in the northwest.
attested_or_hypothetical: ATTESTED language; the relict history is hypothetical
chronological_fit: CANNOT GATE HERE. Requires Elfenbein and the Brahui literature; IH-236 already records that source as named but never read.
geographical_fit: CONSISTENT WITH MEASUREMENT. Brahui sits 393 km from the nearest northwestern lect and 8.6 degrees of longitude west of the next Dravidian language (DE-M-023, DE-M-025). The measurement shows isolation, not how it arose.
contact_mechanism: PASS. Survival of a language island around which the surrounding population shifted is an ordinary, widely observed process.
positive_evidence: The isolation itself; DEDR's inclusion of Brahui as Dravidian (DE-M-013).
contrary_evidence: Not assessed here - it is in the unretrieved literature.
diagnostic_predictions: Archaic retentions shared with Dravidian generally rather than with any one modern branch; no trace of a recent transit corridor.
falsifier: Shared innovations tying Brahui specifically to a modern central or eastern Dravidian branch; a recoverable migration route.
eligible_for_extended_analysis: YES, when the Brahui literature is retrievable
proportional_space: Held open beside HYP-E-007; neither presented as the other's correction.
reason: IH-031 records that the burden was previously inverted on this question. This row does not assert the relict reading; it records that the geography is consistent with it and that the deciding evidence is unretrieved. This is domain M's question, flagged forward rather than pre-empted.

attested_or_hypothetical: ATTESTED language; the migration history is hypothetical

contrary_evidence: IH-031 records that late migration requires an undocumented movement leaving no trace, which is the heavier burden of the two.

reason: IH-156 records that presenting late migration AS the correction was itself rejected. Both Brahui hypotheses are therefore held open together and neither is the default.

exact_claim: The fortified settlements of the Rigveda, named by púr-, durgá-, vr̥trá- and vr̥jána-, are the walled habitations and citadels of the Greater Indus belt across the stages of Harappan urbanisation, and are the nucleus of politically administered territories in the hegemonic conflicts of the Harappan Middle Bronze Age. (R. N. Nandi, 'The City and the Citadel', ch. 4 of An Outline of the Aryan Civilization, Routledge 2017, as its publisher's abstract states it. THE CHAPTER IS NOT READ - SRC-086, SRC-087, HOLD-007, D-046. What is gated is the thesis, not Nandi's argument for it.)
attested_or_hypothetical: Both sides ATTESTED and neither in doubt: the Rigvedic corpus is attested and pinned (SRC-069), and Harappan walled settlements are excavated. HYPOTHETICAL is the IDENTIFICATION of the one with the other. Under the attestation gradient (§4E) this is the third thing - a named historical proposal - and it is not symmetrical with either body of evidence it joins.
chronological_fit: CANNOT BE RUN. The thesis places the Rigvedic fort passages inside Harappan urbanisation, which requires an ABSOLUTE date for the passages. This repository has none: the only chronology in hand is Arnold's relative metrical stratification, single-sourced (DEP-001) and capped at PROVISIONAL where read chronologically (PUR-026). No archaeological source of any kind has been retrieved in this domain. The gate cannot pass or fail this leg, and the honest verdict is that it was not run - NOT that it was passed by default. Note the direction of the risk: the site's own the-forts headline asserts the opposite ('three centuries too late') on no recorded source either, so this repository currently holds an unevidenced chronology on each side.
geographical_fit: CANNOT BE RUN. The pinned corpus carries NO geographic content; the §4J proposed-geography field is typed NOT PRODUCED for that reason. info/rv_locations.tsv, flagged as a candidate in 06-BRIEFS/rv01-reconciliation.md, is a citation-format conversion table. Nothing here places a single púr- passage anywhere.
contact_mechanism: NOT ASSESSED HERE. The thesis needs the Rigvedic composers to be describing Harappan settlements - as occupants, successors, neighbours or observers - and that requires archaeological and chronological evidence this unit has none of. Recorded as unassessed, not as failed.
positive_evidence: ONE OF FOUR TERMS SURVIVES CLEANLY; TWO ARE CONTESTED; AND THE TERM LIST ITSELF IS ON HOLD (DJ-010B). (1) vr̥jána- SUPPORTS the 'politically administered territory' half - glossed 'Gemeinschaft, Territorium einer Gemeinschaft, Niederlassung', 61 tokens. The gloss says a community's TERRITORY; 'politically administered' is Nandi's phrase and the step from one to the other is an untested bridge, not a reading of the gloss. (2) púr- is a wall in the gloss column - 'Wall aus Steinen und Lehm, Verschanzung, Palisade' - but Renou renders it 'forteresses (en briques) crues' at RV 2.35.6 and 'cité' at RV 1.173.10 (DJ-013), so the corpus's own translators do not agree that it is not a city. (3) durgá- is CONTESTED, not failed: the majority of its 21 tokens are difficult ground, but at RV 5.34.7 all three of Griffith, Geldner and Grassmann render a fortified place that people hold out in, and at RV 5.54.4 they disagree (DJ-011, demoted to PROVISIONAL after adversarial review). (4) the vr̥trá- family glosses as resistance and the demon Vr̥tra - and this is the item most likely to be a summariser's garble rather than Nandi's, since it is an odd term for a settlement-name list (DJ-010B). (5) pū́rpati- at RV 1.173.10 is evidence that a fort-lord was an intelligible figure to the audience - one token, inside a simile (DJ-014). It is NOT evidence that a political office is attested: this row said 'names a political office' until re-review, which both overstated a single simile and imported 'political office', an inherited English category of exactly the kind §7 sends for audit, into the row that audits three others.
contrary_evidence: No lemma in the gloss column is glossed 'brick' or 'city', against a denominator of 91.7% of lemmas and 78.98% of tokens (DJ-008), and none is glossed for the act of building (DJ-009). Of the ten passages stating a material, eight are of metal, one of stone and one 'raw/unbaked'; seven of the eight metal forts are not an enemy's, and in two the fort IS something else - Agni at RV 7.15.14, the river Sarasvatī at 7.95.1 (PUR4J finding 4). 3.6% of simplex púr- tokens are locative against 67.5% accusative (DJ-006). The counts behave formulaically rather than enumeratively: Śambara alone carries 90, 99, 100 and 'hundreds', and the ninety-nine expression counts rivers, arms, horses, coils and oblations outside the corpus (DJ-I-01). CAVEATS THAT CUT THE OTHER WAY AND ARE NOT OPTIONAL: RV 2.35.6 applies āmá- 'raw, uncooked' to a púr, the only place the corpus's cooked/raw pair touches a structure (DJ-009); Renou renders pū́rpati- 'maître de la cité' at RV 1.173.10, unbracketed (DJ-013); and the two similes at RV 6.2.7 and 9.107.10 presuppose inhabited forts (DJ-007). TWO EARLIER VERSIONS OF THIS COLUMN WERE WRONG IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS AND BOTH ARE RECORDED. The first typed the brick absence NOT PRODUCED on an unmeasured assertion that the corpus never describes construction technique (BF-017). The second called pakvá-/āmá- 'the fired/unfired opposition brick technology turns on' and cited Renou's bracketed 'briques' as though the text stated a material - the pair is culinary and the brackets are his supplement (BF-018).
independent_support: NONE ESTABLISHED, and the unit's own account of WHY was wrong until adversarial review. Every gloss-based result rests on ONE source - but that source is the Zurich lemma-meaning column (SRC-089, DEP-026), a modern composite citing Geldner, EWAia/Mayrhofer, Scarlata, Oldenberg, Lubotsky, Renou and Kuiper, with Grassmann marked 'GM:' where followed. It is NOT, as this unit repeatedly said, 'one nineteenth-century German lexicon': that phrasing both overstated the weakness of the results against Nandi and understated how much modern apparatus they lean on. Grassmann's actual Worterbuch has never been retrieved here. Griffith, Geldner and Grassmann are three translators in one philological line (DEP-025), and Renou and Elizarenkova were in the pinned clone unread until review (DJ-013). Sāyaṇa is not in the corpus and was not retrieved. There is no non-European scholarly source anywhere in this unit and no archaeological source at all (RA-015, APA-J-002).
source_dependencies: DEP-026 (the gloss column is the Zurich composite, not Grassmann - correcting DEP-005); DEP-005 (lemma and gloss travel together, cap stands, source misnamed); DEP-001 (strata single-sourced); DEP-024 (the four terms are a search-index summary, the glosses are the corpus's - different sources, one each); DEP-025 (Griffith/Geldner/Grassmann are one line); RA-015, RA-018, RA-020.
current_specialist_standing: NOT ESTABLISHED. Step 11 could not be run: the chapter is unread, its citation record is unreachable (api.crossref.org and api.openalex.org both EGRESS_BLOCKED, SRC-087), and no reception literature was retrieved. SRC-088 records that a stronger form of the same thesis is in circulation - dating the Samhitas FROM the fort passages to 3300-2600 BCE - so the position is not a single author's, but how either stands with specialists is unknown here and is not guessed.
diagnostic_predictions: Fixed before the corpus was searched; three of six verdicts CHANGED under adversarial review and all three moved toward the thesis, not away. (P1) a brick word should occur - the gloss column has none, and the two items that moved this leg off FAILS have both weakened on re-review: pakvá-/āmá- is a culinary pair extended to a púr once, and Renou's 'briques' is his bracketed supplement, not the text. The leg is WEAKLY FAILED rather than INCONCLUSIVE - and it cannot be strengthened into a finding either, because the corpus is a hymn corpus and DJ-008's absence is nominal-only. (P2) a term for 'city' should exist - none in the gloss column; Renou renders 'cité' at RV 1.173.10. INCONCLUSIVE. (P3) the four named terms should each denote a fortified settlement - ONE clean support (vr̥jána-), one contested (durgá-), one probably garbled in transmission to us (vr̥trá-), and the list itself on HOLD (DJ-010B). Was recorded as 'FAILS in two of four'; that is withdrawn. (P4) púr- should appear in the locative with human occupants - INCONCLUSIVE: no flat statement, but two similes presuppose it (DJ-007). (P5) a political office attached to a púr should be nameable - PASSES, on one token inside a simile (DJ-014). (P6) counts should be stable per site or opponent if they enumerate real strongholds - FAILS, and this is the one leg that survives review intact (DJ-I-01, PUR4J finding 2).
falsifier: The gate verdict is overturned by obtaining the chapter and finding the argument does not rest on the four-term list its abstract names - or by establishing that the list is not Nandi's at all, which DJ-010B treats as live. It is overturned in the other direction by an archaeological or absolute-chronology source placing any púr- passage in a Harappan settlement. It is SHARPENED, not overturned, by any lexicon or commentary independent of the Zurich gloss column (SRC-089, DEP-026) - Sāyaṇa above all, which would move DJ-010 and DJ-011 off the single column they rest on. Note that this does not require a non-European source: a European translator, Grassmann himself, already contradicts the column's durgá- at RV 5.34.7. This column read 'a single German lexicon' until re-review, which was the withdrawn characterisation and contradicted independent_support in the same row.
proportional_space: A historiographical note, not a section, and not an equal section beside the corpus findings. Step 7 says a hypothesis failing the gate gets a concise exclusion or a historiographical note; this one fails no leg outright on evidence, and fails two legs for want of any evidence at all, which is a different thing and is why the verdict carries SOURCE-BLOCKED rather than NOT-ELIGIBLE. It may be NAMED wherever domain J's public copy discusses what a púr- was, because §4J's prohibition is written against it and a reader meeting the prohibition is owed the position it prohibits. It may NOT be argued for or against at length from this evidence base.
reason: Two of the five gate legs - chronology and geography - CANNOT BE RUN from anything retrieved in this repository, and they are the two the thesis most depends on. Of the legs that could be run, only the counts leg (P6) tells against the thesis without qualification. Adversarial review overturned the two results that had told hardest against it: the durgá- claim was shipped VERIFIED with an absolute quantifier that its own cited translators falsify at RV 5.34.7, and the brick absence was neutralised by an assertion about construction technique that no measurement supported. Both errors ran in the same direction. This is therefore NOT a finding that Nandi is wrong and it must not be reported as one. It is a finding that this repository cannot adjudicate the thesis and can say precisely why: no archaeological source, no absolute chronology, no geography, one gloss column behind every lexical result, and a term list (DJ-010B) that may be a search engine's paraphrase rather than Nandi's. The chapter is paywalled and blocked on both channels - D-046, HOLD-007.
